title: "length() of a data frame counts the columns"
ref: IDX-05
categories: [Indexing]

extrait: 'length(iris)'
reponse: '5'
attendu: "`150`, the number of rows"

---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
length(iris)
nrow(iris)
nrow(1:10)
NROW(1:10)
```
:::

## Why

A data frame is a list of columns. `length()` counts the elements of that list, hence the columns, not the rows.

Conversely, `nrow()` only reads the dimension attribute. A vector has none, hence `NULL`. `NROW()` and `NCOL()`, in capitals, treat a vector as a single column.

## The fix

Say what you are counting: `nrow()` for rows, `ncol()` for columns, and `NROW()` when the object may be a vector or a table.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
nrow(iris)
ncol(iris)
NROW(1:10)
```
:::
